checkpoint: capture uncommitted frozen-v1 state (Context Cards, broadcast extraction, prompt runtime, cache, resume-builder additions)

Everything built since the 2026-08-15 architecture freeze existed only as
uncommitted working-tree changes on jobfynder-intel-01 with no backup or
history. This commit preserves that state as-is on a new branch so it is
durable and reviewable, without altering runtime behavior.

Excludes .env.bak.pre-portkey-removal (left untracked, contains prior
credential values).

feat(hermes-850): add Gmail and Microsoft Graph email provider connectors

Jobfynder receives hotlist/requirement emails on both Gmail and Office 365
mailboxes, not just via a generic inbound-parse webhook. Adds two new
providers following the existing contract-provider pattern (same shape as
whatsapp/slack/teams - code ready, configured:false until real credentials
are supplied):

- app/providers/gmail/service.py: normalize_gmail_message() converts a
  Gmail API users.messages.get resource into the same normalized shape
  app/providers/email/service.py already produces, so it flows through the
  existing, already-verified email intake pipeline (mailbox routing ->
  deterministic hotlist/requirement parsing) unchanged. Also decodes Gmail
  Cloud Pub/Sub push envelopes (historyId only - actual message fetch
  requires HERMES_GMAIL_* credentials, not yet configured).
- app/providers/microsoft_graph/service.py: same pattern for Microsoft
  Graph message resources, including HTML body stripping.
- app/routers/gmail_provider.py: /providers/gmail/status,
  /providers/gmail/push (Pub/Sub push endpoint, always acks).
- app/routers/microsoft_graph_provider.py: /providers/microsoft-graph/status,
  /providers/microsoft-graph/webhook - implements the Graph subscription
  validationToken handshake, required before Graph will ever create a
  subscription against this endpoint.
- app/providers/registry.py: gmail_health()/microsoft_graph_health(),
  registered in PROVIDER_NAMES and GET /providers/status.
- .env.example: HERMES_GMAIL_* and HERMES_MS_GRAPH_* placeholders.
- scripts/hermes-850-gmail-graph-provider-check.py: verifies both
  normalizers against realistic sample payloads (base64url Gmail body
  decoding, HTML-body Graph messages, mailbox routing, and that normalized
  output parses correctly through the existing email_parsing pipeline).

Verified: new checks pass (7/7), existing HERMES-850 checks still pass
(10/10 unit, full email-to-draft integration), app imports cleanly with
103 OpenAPI paths (99 previous + 4 new), /providers/status correctly lists
both as contract/unconfigured.

Not done: no live credentials configured (deliberate - provider choice and
OAuth app registration is pending), so no real email flows through this

Gmail/Graph API to retrieve the actual message) is not implemented -
normalize_gmail_message()/normalize_graph_message() are ready for it, the
authenticated fetch call itself is the remaining piece once credentials
exist.

feat(hermes-850): implement the fetch-from-provider step for Gmail/Graph

Closes the one gap HERMES-850's own closure doc (§7) named as the real
remaining work: the connector code (normalize_gmail_message,
normalize_graph_message) and webhook endpoints existed and were tested
against sample payloads, but neither push/webhook handler actually called
out to the provider's API to fetch the message that changed -- they just
acknowledged the notification and stopped.

Gmail (app/providers/gmail/service.py):
- fetch_new_gmail_messages(notification_history_id): Pub/Sub push only
  carries the mailbox's CURRENT historyId, not a delta, so finding what
  actually changed requires calling history.list with startHistoryId set
  to the LAST historyId Hermes processed. That cursor is persisted at
  /hermes-runtime/gmail/history_cursor.json via the existing
  app.runtime.jsonl_store helpers (same mechanism app/drafts/service.py
  already uses). First-ever notification for a mailbox has no prior
  cursor -- stores it as the baseline and returns [] rather than
  guessing at history from before Hermes started watching.
- Refresh-token OAuth exchange + authenticated messages.get, using
  stdlib urllib (Request/urlopen) to match this codebase's existing
  outbound-HTTP convention (see app/providers/linkedin/service.py,
  app/providers/telegram/service.py) rather than introducing a new HTTP
  client dependency.
- Never raises: missing credentials or any API failure returns [] --
  Pub/Sub redelivers on non-2xx, so failing the whole webhook response
  would cause duplicate delivery, not recovery.

Microsoft Graph (app/providers/microsoft_graph/service.py):
- fetch_graph_message(resource): app-only (client-credentials) token
  acquisition + a direct GET of the notification's own `resource` field
  against Graph v1.0. App-only, not delegated, since there's no
  interactive user in a webhook handler -- requires the app registration
  to have been granted Mail.Read as an *application* permission,
  admin-consented in Azure AD (a console step, not something this code
  can do). Same never-raises contract as the Gmail fetch.

Both routers (gmail_provider.py, microsoft_graph_provider.py) now call
fetch -> normalize_*_message() -> process_channel_intake() for each
notification, the exact same pipeline /providers/email/webhook already
uses, and report per-message intake_status/document_kind/draft_object_type
in the response instead of just acknowledging.

Also fixed, found while reading this code: app/routers/drafts.py had NO
permission dependency on any of its 3 routes (list/read/publish an
extracted draft), unlike every comparable Core-facing router in this
codebase (resume_builder.py, jobs.py both gate via
Depends(require_permission(...))). Added drafts:read/drafts:publish,
matching the established pattern. RBAC_ENFORCEMENT defaults to disabled,
so this is a no-op until an operator enables it and grants those
permissions to whichever token Core uses.

feat(drafts): add reject_draft_object, mirroring publish

Needed by Core's draft-review workflow: a reviewer needs a way to
dismiss a draft that doesn't warrant creating a real Core record (e.g.
a hotlist or profile draft, since Core-side auto-creation of those was
explicitly scoped out) without leaving it stuck in a pending-forever
state. DraftStatus already had "rejected" as a valid value in
app/drafts/models.py; nothing previously set it.

POST /drafts/{draft_id}/reject accepts an optional {reason: string},
stored in the draft's metadata, and emits a draft.rejected event
alongside the existing draft.created/draft.published ones. Same
drafts:publish permission as the publish route -- rejecting is the same
class of reviewer action as publishing, not a lesser one.

feat(hermes-850): Graph subscription lifecycle + clientState verification

The fetch step added earlier this pass only handles reacting to a push
notification -- neither Gmail nor Graph will ever send one unless
something first registers a watch/subscription, and Graph's own
subscriptions for mail expire after ~2.94 days max. Nothing previously
created or renewed one, so notifications would never have started
flowing even with real credentials configured. Scoped to Graph only for
this pass (Gmail deferred).

app/providers/microsoft_graph/service.py:
- sync_graph_subscriptions(): creates a subscription for every mailbox in
  HERMES_MS_GRAPH_MAILBOXES that doesn't have one, renews (PATCH
  expirationDateTime) any expiring within 24h, leaves already-fresh ones
  alone. Persists subscription id + expiry at
  /hermes-runtime/microsoft_graph/subscriptions.json (same
  app.runtime.jsonl_store mechanism used elsewhere). Access token is
  acquired lazily -- only if at least one mailbox actually needs an API
  call this run, not unconditionally.
- Reuses the existing HERMES_PUBLIC_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL var (already used by
  the Telegram provider) to build the notification URL, rather than
  adding a redundant new one.
- verify_notification_client_state(): closes a real security gap found
  while building this -- the webhook handler had no way to distinguish a
  genuine Graph notification from a forged POST to the (necessarily
  unauthenticated) public webhook URL. Graph's own mechanism is
  clientState: a secret set at subscription-creation time that every
  notification for that subscription echoes back. The webhook now
  rejects (skips fetching) any notification whose clientState doesn't
  match HERMES_MS_GRAPH_CLIENT_STATE, and treats an unconfigured secret
  as "reject everything," not "skip the check."

app/routers/microsoft_graph_provider.py: adds
POST /providers/microsoft-graph/subscriptions/sync (admin-gated via the
existing require_permission, matching drafts.py's pattern from earlier

scripts/hermes-850-graph-subscription-renew.py: the actual production
requirement here -- meant to run from a daily host cron
(docker exec hermes-api python scripts/...). Without this running on a

Verified: all 3 pre-existing HERMES-850 scripts still pass unchanged (10

feat(hermes-850): confidence-based hotlist/requirement classification for a shared mailbox

Jobfynder's real deployment uses one inbox (jobs@jobfynder.com) for both
hotlist and requirement email, not the two separate addresses
app/email_parsing/routing.py's classify_recipient_mailbox() was built
around. Pointing HOTH HERMES_HOTLIST_MAILBOX and
HERMES_REQUIREMENTS_MAILBOX at jobs@jobfynder.com would make every
message double-match and return "unknown"; leaving them at their
original (different, non-matching) defaults gets the same "unknown"
result for the real inbox, either way losing the recipient-address
signal detect_document_kind() relied on to tell the two apart.

app/email_parsing/parsers.py: adds classify_email_by_confidence(text).
Runs BOTH parse_hotlist_email() and parse_requirement_email() -- each
already does real structural analysis (table-row detection, labeled-
field extraction) to produce its own confidence score -- and keeps
whichever wins, gated behind two thresholds calibrated against this
module's own fixtures:
- CLASSIFICATION_MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.70, same threshold the parsers
  already use for requires_review) -- the winner has to be a
  confident match on its own, not just the less-bad of two mediocre
  guesses.
- CLASSIFICATION_MIN_MARGIN (0.15) -- the winner has to clear the loser
  by a real margin. This one mattered in practice: both parsers'
  fallback paths assign SOME confidence to almost any non-empty text
  (they always emit a record, just review-flagged, rather than refusing
  to guess), so unrelated text scored 0.30 vs 0.35 in testing -- a
  bare tie-check would have "classified" ordinary correspondence as a
  job requirement. Real hotlist/requirement fixtures score ~0.90 on
  their own parser vs. ~0.60 on the other (margin ~0.30), well clear of
  both thresholds.

app/channels/service.py: detect_document_kind() calls this before
falling through to the existing generic keyword-marker classification,
but only for email where intended_document_kind (recipient-address
routing) didn't already resolve definitively.

.env.example: documents HERMES_MS_GRAPH_MAILBOXES=jobs@jobfynder.com as
the real value, and explains why HERMES_HOTLIST_MAILBOX/
HERMES_REQUIREMENTS_MAILBOX must NOT be changed to match it.

Verified: all pre-existing HERMES-850 scripts still pass unchanged.
Extended hermes-850-email-parsing-check.py with 4 new unit-level checks

feat(hermes-850): resolve original sender for forwarded email (spec 4.1)

Forwarded-mail sources (e.g. a recruiter mailing list relaying postings
instead of sending/CC-ing directly) carry the forwarder address on the
outer From header, not the recruiter who actually wrote the message. Any
future claim-and-verify flow that emails the sender back needs the real
recruiter, not the relay -- resolve it deterministically before that step
exists, so it is not a retrofit later.

Resolution order: forwarded-message header block in the body, then
Reply-To, then a contact email found elsewhere in the body. None resolving
does not guess -- returns a null candidate instead of a wrong recipient.

Wired into normalize_email_payload() as metadata.original_sender_candidate,
populated only when the body looks forwarded; direct-send mail is
untouched. No LLM involved.

feat(hermes-850): exact-content dedupe, field provenance, claim-and-verify loop

Closes the remaining spec gaps on top of the forwarded-sender resolution
commit: exact-content deduplication, field-level provenance, and the
claim-and-verify loop that turns a parsed job requirement into a
recruiter-confirmed, published listing.

Exact-content dedupe (app/email_parsing/dedupe.py): a raw-body sha256
index catches the same content arriving under a different
provider_message_id (e.g. forwarded to two aliases) -- distinct from the
existing transport-level duplicate_key check, which only catches retries
of the same id. Never drops a message; every source email still gets its
own draft, just linked to the first-seen one via duplicate_group_id.

Field provenance (app/email_parsing/provenance.py): every job-requirement
and hotlist-consultant field the deterministic parser extracts gets its
own row (field_path, extractor, extraction_method, confidence, value_kind)
persisted per draft. A recruiter correction during claim becomes a new
row tagged extractor=recruiter_correction rather than overwriting the
original -- this is the free accuracy-labeling signal the claim loop is
for.

Claim-and-verify (app/claim/): prepare_claim() resolves the real
recruiter contact (forwarded-sender candidate, then direct sender, then
a body-text contact email -- never guesses) and builds a token-linked,
14-day-expiring claim with a deterministic email template. Hermes never
sends the email itself (email_provider_status().supports_outbound stays
False) -- it hands Core/n8n the subject/body/link to actually deliver,
per the existing Hermes-decides/Core-executes boundary. confirm_claim()
records any corrections as provenance, merges them onto the draft, and
publishes it. New router: POST /claim/prepare, GET /claim/{token},
POST /claim/{token}/confirm, POST /claim/{claim_id}/mark-sent.

Also fixes a gap the sender-resolution commit left open:
process_channel_intake() never forwarded request.sender or
request.metadata onto the created draft, so original_sender_candidate
was computed but silently lost before claim resolution could ever see
it. Now carried through, with sender-resolution recomputed from
request.text as a channel-level fallback so it holds regardless of
which entry point normalized the payload.

Verified against the real hermes-api container image: all 8
hermes-850-*-check.py scripts pass, including the two untouched by this
change (gmail-graph-provider-check, live-fetch-check) -- zero
regressions. New coverage: hermes-850-dedupe-check.py,
hermes-850-provenance-check.py, hermes-850-claim-check.py (full
prepare -> confirm -> publish round trip, blocked-on-no-contact,
blocked-on-wrong-draft-type, expired-claim cases).
